structure.note: Mastercard has Class A common stock (877,780,670 shares outstanding on April 21, 2026, per the proxy), its only voting class, and non-voting Class B common stock held only by certain customers (6,519,005 shares on October 26, 2026, per the Q3 2026 10-Q cover). The proxy says Class B accounts for less than 1% of total outstanding equity and is not publicly traded. Class B converts one-for-one into Class A. No holder controls the company.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Documents read on sec.gov: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001141391-26-000013, filed February 11, 2026) and the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001141391-26-000021, filed April 27, 2026). AJAY BANGA was CEO until 2020; the 2026 proxy mentions him only in the pay-versus-performance footnote for 2021 (a non-PEO named executive officer). He is not a director or named executive officer and does not appear in its ownership tables, so status is no-reported-stake. HOLDER PERCENTAGES are as the proxy states them: percent of Class A common stock outstanding (877,780,670 shares on April 21, 2026). Class B (under 1% of total equity) is not in the denominator, so the stated figures are very slightly above each holder's share of all shares. asOf for each holder is the Schedule 13G/A filing date the proxy cites. Vanguard and BlackRock still rest on February 2024 filings and are stale; the proxy adds that Vanguard reported on a Schedule 13G/A of March 27, 2026 that, after an internal realignment, it no longer has beneficial ownership over shares held by various Vanguard subsidiaries and business divisions, which will report separately. The Foundation's stake fell from 84.8 million to 65.2 million shares (9.4% to 7.4%) per its April 16, 2026 Schedule 13G/A; its type is 'other' (a Canadian charitable foundation's asset manager). The proxy states each director and executive officer, and the group, owns less than 1% of Class A. The ESPP is recorded from the 10-K exhibit index; the 10-K gives no participation figures.

ecosystem.notes: The FY2025 10-K states GDV rounded, as $10.6T. It also gives three program rows for 2025 (Consumer Credit $3,878B, Consumer Debit and Prepaid $5,349B, Commercial Credit and Debit $1,405B), which were not added up. GDV is the spend on Mastercard-branded cards, and the 10-K notes that the GDV data is 'provided by Mastercard customers'. Mastercard is a network, not a marketplace: issuing banks, acquirers and merchants keep most of the economics, so net revenue divided by GDV is a network fee rate, not a share of the sale. GDV excludes Maestro and Cirrus.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Mastercard net revenue includes value-added services and solutions that are not charged on gross dollar volume, so net revenue ÷ GDV is not a like-for-like share.

taxes.notes: Taxes: income taxes paid, net of refunds, from the FY2025 10-K income-tax note by jurisdiction (federal 1,359, state 95, foreign: Belgium 668, United Kingdom 330, Brazil 168, other 400; total 3,020 million). R&D is not reported as a separate line in the FY2025 10-K.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001141391-26-000013). Payment network: formula applies with the sector flag. Net revenue is after rebates and incentives granted to customers (contra-revenue), so those payments to issuers and merchants are not in paidOut; operating cash flow carries them through prepaid expenses (−3,388) and amortization of customer incentives (2,098). No acquisitions of businesses in 2025. Interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow; under the new income-tax disclosure the 10-K no longer prints a supplemental cash-flow line, so taxes come from the income-tax note's by-jurisdiction table and interest from the debt note (the filing tags that interest-paid sentence as us-gaap:InterestExpenseDebt).

owners.notes: NBIM: the quote is this company's equity row in NBIM's holdings data file at June 30, 2026 ("o" = ownership %, "eq.v" = voting %, "a.e" = market value in USD, "a.n" = in NOK); NBIM also holds Mastercard corporate bonds, in a separate row that is not counted. Form 13F covers only U.S.-listed securities, and the quoted row gives issuer, class, CUSIP, value in dollars and shares. CalPERS holds Class A; the percentage divides its September 30, 2026 shares by Class A plus Class B at October 26, 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover), the same count used in the marketcap lens. pay.notes: Employees: approximate year-end count from the FY2025 10-K; the 10-K says the employee base is predominantly full-time and that Mastercard also had about 6,000 contingent workers, who are not counted. Payroll: the Personnel line of general and administrative expenses in the MD&A. The 10-K's human-capital section separately states "The total cost of our workforce for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $7.3 billion, which primarily consists of compensation, benefits and other personnel-related costs." The 2026 proxy reports a 2025 median employee annual total compensation of $124,650 (CEO pay ratio 284 to 1), not used because a total is disclosed.
